To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

indocyanine inhibits the hepato-specific uptake of Gd ethoxybenzyloxyethoxybenzyldithylenetriamine penta-acetic acid, which is used in magnetic resonance imaging, and that this inhibition is more obvious in hypothermal mice.
indocyanine-green injection decreases the peak contrast ratio of Gd-ethoxybenzyldiglycolic acid (Gd-EoB) in the liver of mice.
indocyanine-green injection decreases the peak liver enhancement in Gd-EOBDTPA-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging in mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between ICG and Gd-EOBDTPA.
the interaction between ICG and Gd-EOBDTPA and the influence of temperature.
the influence of ICG on Gd-EO-B-DTPA–based magnetic resonance imaging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in hypothermic animals, Gd-EOBDTPA uptake is inhibited by ICG, whereas in normothermic mice the effect is less pronounced.
ICG inhibits Gd-EOBDTPA uptake in a dose-dependent and temperature-dependent manner.
ICG can affect the signal intensity of Gd-EBOD-DTPA–based liver MRI and that the effect is more pronounced in hypothermic animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypothermia and ICG can affect the hepatic uptake and signal intensity of Gd-BOPTA.
ICG inhibits the hepetic uptake of Gd-Eob-DTPA and affect the signal intensity of Gd-EOB-DTPA enhanced MRI.
ICG inhibits the hepato-specific uptake of Gd-DTPA-EOB in mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the influence of ICG on Gd-EO-B-DTPA uptake should be taken into consideration when ICG and Gd-EO-DTPA are used in the same patient.
ICG and Gd-EOBDTPA should not be administered in the same session.
the influence of ICG should be taken into account when performing Gd-EOBDTPA–enhancement magnetic resonance imaging.
